title: Lam's supply-constraint warning triggers a chip selloff as Meta's capex outruns its cash flow
intro: Demand signals stayed strong, with record results at Lam, Micron's HBM sold out for 2026 and BofA projecting data-center spending to double by 2028, but Lam's warning that component shortages capped its outlook and Meta's negative free cash flow on heavy capex sent chip and equipment stocks sharply lower. Tracked value fell 4.4% between the Oct 19 and Oct 23 closes, led by energy, equipment and optics, while the server makers held up best.
movers_note: Between the Oct 19 and Oct 23 closes (Oct 22 for Taiwan listings) Lam Research (-15.5%), Credo (-14.8%), Bloom Energy (-14.6%), KLA (-12.5%) and SUMCO (-11.7%) fell most, while Super Micro (+2.6%), Quanta Computer (+2.4%), Foxconn (+2.3%), Dell (+0.2%) and SK hynix (0.0%) were the only names not to decline.

items.headline: Chip stocks sink as Lam flags near-term supply-chain constraints
items.summary: Lam's CFO said the $8.6B December guide would have been higher without short-term component constraints. Lam fell as much as 11% and the semiconductor index dropped over 6%, with Marvell down 9%, AMAT and Intel 7% each, ASML 6% and Broadcom over 4%.

items.headline: Lam Research posts record $8.22B quarter, guides December to $8.6B
items.summary: Lam's September-quarter revenue rose 22% sequentially and about 54% year on year, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.20 and China at 35% of sales. December guidance is $8.60B plus or minus $400M, with gross margin guided at 52.5%.

items.headline: Meta narrows 2026 capex to $135-145B as quarterly spending outruns cash flow
items.summary: Meta reported Q3 revenue of $64.6B (up 26%) and raised the low end of 2026 capex to $135B from $130B, with the top unchanged at $145B. Quarterly capex of $34.91B exceeded operating cash flow of $32.79B, leaving free cash flow at negative $2.12B; shares fell almost 8% the next day.

items.headline: OpenAI nears up to $30B raise at $1.25T valuation, possibly paired with UAE compute
items.summary: Reports say OpenAI is negotiating a round of up to $30B at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, led by Coatue with UAE investors. The funding could come with a deal for more computing capacity from the UAE, though no terms were given and details may change.

items.headline: Micron maps a new HBM generation each year through 2030; 2026 supply sold out
items.summary: At an Oct 21 webinar Micron laid out HBM4 in 2026, HBM4E in 2027, HBM5 in 2028 and HBM6 in 2030. Its entire 2026 HBM supply is sold out, it targets roughly 20% HBM share by year-end, and its Singapore packaging site should add capacity in the first half of 2027.

items.headline: BofA sees data-center spending near $1T in 2026 and over $2.1T by 2028
items.summary: A BofA Global Research note, as reported by Reuters, puts 2026 global data-center spending near $1 trillion and over $2.1 trillion in 2028. It estimates build cost at about $49M per megawatt, with servers the largest line item at about $31.4M per megawatt and networking next at about $4.8M.

items.headline: SK hynix's Solidigm shelves IPO plans, citing capital-market conditions
items.summary: SK hynix said its Solidigm NAND unit has stopped reviewing a pre-IPO round and listing, pointing to current capital-market conditions. The disclosure came as Korean memory shares opened after the overnight US chip selloff.

items.headline: Texas Instruments Q3 revenue rises 28% to $6.06B, naming data centers as a driver
items.summary: TI's third-quarter revenue was $6.06B with EPS of $2.62, and the CEO named industrial, automotive and data center as growth areas. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance is $5.80B to $6.30B.
